questions.q: What lets a driver slow down gradually, instead of braking hard at the last moment?
options: Looking far ahead and keeping a large gap from the vehicle in front
Listening to loud music
Always driving at the maximum permitted speed
Driving close behind the vehicle in front
questions.explain: A driver who looks far ahead and keeps a gap spots the need to slow down early, and can ease off the accelerator gradually instead of braking hard.

questions.q: What is "coasting correctly" when approaching a red light?
options: Braking hard the moment you see the red light
Shifting to neutral well before the light
Accelerating up to the light and then braking hard
Easing off the accelerator early, in gear, without braking too early and without accelerating until the last moment
questions.explain: Correct coasting is done in gear, not in neutral — this keeps you in control of the vehicle throughout the slowdown.

questions.q: When is cruise control best suited for use?
options: On a long drive on an open, non-urban road, at a steady speed
On a mountain road with frequent climbs and descents
In heavy rain and on a slippery road
In dense urban traffic
questions.explain: Cruise control saves fuel when driving at a steady speed on the open road; it is less suited to changing conditions.

questions.q: Why does driving faster on a non-urban road generally use more fuel per kilometre?
options: Because air resistance grows roughly with the square of the speed
Because the engine gets hotter
Because cruise control does not work at high speed
Because the tyres get hot
questions.explain: Aerodynamic drag grows sharply with speed, so fuel consumption per kilometre rises significantly at higher speeds.

questions.q: What happens when tyre pressure is lower than recommended?
options: The tyre cools down and performs better
Fuel consumption rises and the tyre's life is shortened
Fuel consumption falls
It has no effect at all
questions.explain: A tyre with low pressure increases rolling resistance, which increases fuel consumption — and wears out faster.

questions.q: How does a roof box affect fuel consumption, especially at high speed?
options: It has no effect at all
It only affects oil consumption
It increases air resistance and therefore fuel consumption
It reduces fuel consumption
questions.explain: A roof box increases air resistance, so it especially affects fuel consumption when driving fast.

questions.q: Under regulation 72A, what is allowed regarding running the engine of a parked bus before passengers board?
options: The engine may be run at all times, without restriction
The engine may never be run under any circumstances
It may not be run, except to build up air in the pneumatic system, or for up to {{fact:eco.bus_idle_before_boarding_max_min}} before boarding
It may only be run at night
questions.explain: Regulation 72A forbids starting the engine of a parked bus until passengers board, except to build up air in the pneumatic system, or for up to {{fact:eco.bus_idle_before_boarding_max_min}} in advance.

questions.q: Which of the following increases fuel consumption?
options: Engine oil that was recently changed
Working spark plugs
A clean air filter
A clogged air filter or worn spark plugs
questions.explain: Neglected maintenance — a clogged filter or worn spark plugs — makes it harder for the engine to work efficiently and increases fuel consumption.

questions.q: Why is it better to combine several errands into one trip, instead of several separate short trips?
options: Because short trips damage the engine
Because it lowers the price of insurance
There is no difference in fuel consumption
Because a cold engine uses more fuel per kilometre in the first minutes of every trip
questions.explain: A cold engine uses more fuel, so several short cold trips cost more fuel than one combined trip.

questions.q: Why does driving in a jam generally use more fuel per kilometre than flowing driving?
options: Because the tyres get hotter in a jam
Because every stop and restart requires acceleration that burns fuel
Because the air conditioner works harder in a jam
There is no difference in fuel consumption between a jam and flowing driving
questions.explain: Repeated stop-and-start burns more fuel than driving at a steady speed, even over the same distance.

questions.q: What is special about regenerative braking in an electric vehicle?
options: It deliberately heats up the battery
It is only available at very high speed
It returns some of the vehicle's kinetic energy to the battery, instead of wasting it as heat in the brakes
It switches the vehicle off completely
questions.explain: Regenerative braking converts some of the kinetic energy back into electricity, charging the battery in the process.

Parking in a forbidden place
Driving without a seatbelt
Driving a vehicle that emits gases, smoke, oil or fuel beyond what is normal, in a way that bothers road users or endangers safety
questions.explain: Regulation 155 forbids driving or leaving standing a vehicle that emits substances beyond what is normal for its kind.

questions.q: What is the fine for misusing the horn?
options: {{fine:horn-misuse}}
{{fine:parking-general-prohibited-sign}}
{{fine:continuous-line}}
There is no fine for this
questions.explain: Misusing the horn is a separate fixed-fine offence (regulation 63), with a fine of {{fine:horn-misuse}}.

questions.q: What does regulation 157 say about noise?
options: Vehicle noise is always allowed, at any level
You must not drive a vehicle that makes excessive noise from a fault, neglected maintenance or a badly arranged load; on an urban road only the noise needed for it to run properly is allowed
Noise is only allowed for an electric vehicle
Vehicle noise is forbidden only at night
questions.explain: Regulation 157 forbids excessive noise caused by a fault, neglect or a load, and limits urban noise to what is needed.

questions.q: Why is thick smoke coming from a vehicle also a safety risk, not just harm to the environment?
options: It lowers the price of fuel
It cools the engine too much
It improves tyre grip
It blocks the view of drivers behind the vehicle
questions.explain: Thick smoke harms the visibility of anyone driving behind the vehicle, not only pollutes the air.
